title: Hurricane Helene
subtitle: 23–29 September 2024, southeastern United States
source: ERA5 reanalysis (Hersbach et al. 2020), Copernicus Climate Change Service, via ARCO-ERA5 on Google Cloud

markers.title: A storm organizes
markers.text: Helene takes shape over the warm northwestern Caribbean, embedded in a deep reservoir of tropical moisture.

markers.title: Rain arrives before the storm
markers.text: A predecessor rain event sets up over the southern Appalachians, soaking soils a day before Helene's core arrives.

markers.title: Landfall in the Big Bend
markers.text: Helene makes landfall in Florida's Big Bend as a major hurricane and races north toward a cutoff low over the Tennessee Valley.

markers.title: Flooding in western North Carolina
markers.text: Moist southeasterly flow is forced up the Blue Ridge escarpment. Rain on already saturated ground drives catastrophic flooding.

markers.title: Absorbed by the cutoff low
markers.text: Helene's remnants merge with the upper-level low and the rain shield weakens.
